tags.description:en: The newest part of the village, bordering Novе Selo. Built in the late 1980s to resettle people from the Chornobyl exclusion zone. The name also applies to a shop near Novе Selo.
tags.name: Чорнобильський куток

tags.description: Новіша частина села, збудована в 60-х роках ХХ століття для відселення людей з села Комарівка, у звʼязку з будівництвом Канівської гідроелектростанції.
tags.description:en: The newer part of the village, built in the 1960s to resettle people from the village of Komarivka due to the construction of the Kaniv Hydroelectric Power Station.
tags.description:uk: Новіша частина села, збудована в 60-х роках ХХ століття для відселення людей з села Комарівка, у звʼязку з будівництвом Канівської гідроелектростанції.
tags.name: Нове Село

tags.description:en: Dudurivshchyna is the southern part of the village. The name comes from the surname Dudura. Until the 1960s, it was a pasture, now planted with pine. Locals often suffered from sandstorms—some say even their borscht had sand in it.
tags.name: Дудурівщина

tags.description:en: The toponym emerged in the 1960s when a collective farm apiary was established in the area.
tags.name: Пасіка

tags.description:en: Dubyna is located 300 m southwest of the village, in the forest. This area is covered exclusively with oak trees, which is the origin of the place name. The oak species is the common or English oak (Quercus robur L.).
tags.name: Дубина

tags.description:en: The name comes from the name of a local resident, Samson Plotka. His household stood on this hill. The toponym originated in the early 20th century.
tags.name: Самсонів Горб

tags.description:en: Bahny is the southern part of the village, bordered by forest to the south and west. At its centre lies a lake of the same name, over 40 m in diameter, clearly visible on topographic maps. The name comes from the Ukrainian word bahno—swamp, bog, or mire.
tags.name: Багни

tags.description:en: The name also refers to large uninhabited areas and irregular corners, mostly formed in the 1930s. Before the Holodomor, these lands held peasant households, but after entire families perished, no one ever settled here again.
tags.name: Вигон

tags.description:en: Likely a remnant of an old riverbed. This 150 m oval lake, spring-fed, lies in a gully running west to east toward the Brovarka River. Locals say a bell from the Church of Archangel Michael, burned by the Germans in 1943, rolled into it.
tags.name: Ставок

tags.description:en: The western part of a gully-like depression of an ancient riverbed. The name comes from the word “saha” (swampy lowland).
tags.name: Сажалка

tags.description:en: Voshynyi Khutir is the western part of the village, located on sandy soil unsuitable for farming. After a hospital was built there in 1867 by the Russian Insurance Society, the area became known as “Bolnychna”.
tags.name: Больнична

tags.description:en: The western part of the old village, bordering the Old Cemetery. This area was burned down by the Germans in 1943. The name comes from the surname Shanko.
tags.name: Шанькове

tags.description:en: The main northern part of the village. At its centre lies a lake of the same name, over 80 m in diameter. The name comes from the term meaning “to settle”, referring to creating a home in a new place. The area was settled in the early 20th century.
tags.name: Селище

tags.description:en: Zaiacha is the northern part of the village. The name applies to a street bordering the fields and originates from the surname Zaiets, common among the residents there.
tags.name: Заяча
